content.heading: FROM WORKFLOW FRICTION TO VALIDATED SYSTEMS
content.tagline: Cross-functional engineering workflows translated into reliable, scalable software platforms.

slides.title: Where Risk Enters the Workflow
slides.subtitle: When system logic is fragmented, friction appears at every stage of design and delivery.
slides.takeaway: When validation happens late, friction multiplies across the workflow.

notes.intent: Demonstrate that 'friction' is a structural workflow problem, not just an organizational one.
notes.summary: Show where risk enters the engineering workflow when complex systems are designed using fragmented logic.

content.caption: "Fragmented logic shifts validation downstream and multiplies risk."

slides.title: How I Build Internal Platforms
slides.subtitle: A cross-functional workflow from concept → deployment.
slides.takeaway: Alignment + validation + iteration is what makes tools scalable.

notes.intent: Demonstrate operational rigor and empathy for the end-user (engineer/designer).
notes.summary: I follow a formal product lifecycle even for internal tools. This includes immersion with project engineers, prototyping with calc designers, and validation sprints with test groups.

slides.title: Powerful Products. Complex Systems.
slides.subtitle: Engineering excellence introduces configuration complexity.
slides.takeaway: As product capability increases, structured tooling becomes necessary to reduce risk and variability.

notes.intent: Demonstrate product depth understanding and set up case studies as necessary solutions—not optional tools.
notes.summary: Increased product capability naturally results in system-level configuration density. Structured engineering platforms are necessary to translate this complexity into consistent, risk-mitigated outputs.

slides.title: Encoding Engineering Judgment
slides.subtitle: Case Study 1: From manual variance to rule-based validation
slides.takeaway: When requirements become code, outputs become consistent — and risk shifts upstream.

notes.intent: Prove that automation here means structural risk reduction, not just calculation speed.
notes.summary: Demonstrates the transition from spreadsheet-based logic to an encoded rules engine with real-time validation and standardized outputs.

slides.title: From Tool to Platform
slides.subtitle: Project-Level Orchestration
slides.takeaway: Project-level hierarchy turns many enclosures into one consistent BOM and documentation set.

notes.intent: Highlight the shift from single-system validation to project-wide coordination and repeatable deliverables.
notes.summary: Shows how enclosure → zone → system → project aggregation enables cross-zone validation and standardized outputs.

slides.title: Small Automation, Big Leverage
slides.subtitle: Case Study 3: Eliminating a high-frequency bottleneck
slides.takeaway: Automating the decisions made 40 times creates more impact than optimizing the ones made once.

notes.intent: Show that structured thinking scales from large platforms down to small, high-frequency workflows.
notes.summary: Illustrates how targeted automation of repetitive calculations reduces engineering gatekeeping and accelerates quoting.

content.problemDescription: Engineers repeatedly filtered bracket compatibility across matrices and PDF references.
